extraction.name: SciQ
extraction.description: A dataset of 13.7K multiple choice science exam questions crowdsourced using a two-step process involving domain-specific text and existing questions. The dataset includes a multiple choice version (selecting the correct answer from options) and a direct answer version (predicting the span within a passage that answers the question).
extraction.creator: Johannes Welbl, Nelson F. Liu, Matt Gardner
extraction.citeAs: Welbl, J., Liu, N. F., & Gardner, M. (2017). Crowdsourcing Multiple Choice Science Questions. arXiv preprint arXiv:1707.06209.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was crowdsourced using a two-step process: (1) crowd workers selected relevant passages from domain-specific textbooks and generated questions based on them, and (2) another set of crowd workers validated the questions and generated plausible answer distractors with the aid of a model trained to predict good distractors. The base corpus consisted of 28 science study textbooks from various online learning resources, including CK-12 and OpenStax, under Creative Commons licenses. A rule-based document filter was applied to select suitable paragraphs for question generation. The process involved 175 crowd workers on Amazon Mechanical Turk, with a total budget of $10,415.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Experiments
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Science study textbooks from CK-12 and OpenStax, covering biology, chemistry, earth science, and physics, spanning elementary to college introductory levels.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The crowdsourcing process was conducted over a period of time with a total budget of $10,415, resulting in 13,679 multiple choice science questions.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A rule-based document filter was applied to individual paragraphs to select sentences suitable for generating questions. The filter included lexical, grammatical, pragmatical, and complexity-based rules to exclude irrelevant or unsuitable text (e.g., questions, exclamations, imperative phrases, personal pronouns, special characters, and instructional vocabulary).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowd workers were instructed to generate questions based on selected passages, ensuring they were relevant to science exams, not requiring further context, and querying general principles rather than highly specific facts. Workers were also tasked with validating questions and generating plausible answer distractors, with the aid of a model trained to predict good distractors.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Workers were required to validate questions and select or generate answer distractors. The process included quality control steps where workers judged whether questions could appear in school science exams and selected up to two of the six suggested distractors, writing at least one distractor themselves.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 (one correct answer and two distractors selected by workers, with at least one distractor generated by the worker)
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: 175 crowd workers on Amazon Mechanical Turk, all required to have Master's status. The task was advertised on Amazon Mechanical Turk, and workers were compensated ($0.30 per HIT for question generation and $0.20 per HIT for distractor selection).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: A random forest model trained to predict plausible answer distractors based on features such as GloVe embeddings, POS-tag consistency, singular/plural consistency, word frequency, Levenshtein distance, suffix consistency, token overlap, and WordNet-based hypernymy indicators.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is released under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 3.0 Unported (CC BY-NC 3.0) license. The dataset is available at http://allenai.org/data.html and is intended for research purposes. The authors mention potential future work to improve document selection, question generation, and distractor prediction to generate questions fully automatically.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to improve science exam question answering models, which could have broader implications for educational AI systems. The method addresses the challenge of creating high-quality, domain-targeted multiple choice questions, which is crucial for advancing AI in specialized domains like science education.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may reflect biases present in the source textbooks (e.g., Simple Wikipedia articles and OpenStax/CK-12 textbooks), which may not cover all aspects of science education equally. The crowdsourcing process may also introduce biases based on the selection of crowd workers and their interpretations of the guidelines for question and distractor generation.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to science exam questions and may not generalize to other domains. The multiple choice version of the dataset does not include the associated passage, requiring systems to retrieve their own background knowledge. The direct answer version excludes a small percentage of passages due to unreleasable texts. The dataset may also have limitations in terms of question diversity and complexity, as it relies on the source textbooks and the crowdsourcing guidelines provided to workers.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning. The dataset is intended for research in science question answering, reading comprehension, and neural model performance in medium-sized data settings. It can also be used as additional training data to improve performance on real science exams.
